stem:
The resistors \(R_1\), \(R_2\), \(R_3\) and \(R_4\) in the given circuit are all equal in value and connected with a negligible-resistance wire. Which of the following is the correct relationship between the voltmeter readings \(V_1\), \(V_2\) and \(V_3\)?

(The figure shows four equal resistors \(R_1\), \(R_2\), \(R_3\), \(R_4\) connected in series in a single loop across a 12 V battery. Three voltmeters are connected in the top wire: \(V_1\) reads the potential difference across \(R_1\), \(V_2\) reads across \(R_2\), and \(V_3\) reads across \(R_3\) and \(R_4\) together.)

The following graph was plotted between V and I values across a metal wire. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct regarding this?

(The graph plots V (volt) on the y-axis against I (ampere) on the x-axis. The plot is a single straight line passing through the origin, rising linearly through points such as I = 0.2 A, 0.4 A, 0.6 A.)

options.label: A
options.text: This graph illustrates the non-ohmic law.

options.label: B
options.text: While plotting this graph, the temperature remains constant.

options.label: C
options.text: The value of ratio \(\frac{V}{I}\) when the potential difference is 0.8 V is not equal to the value of ratio \(\frac{V}{I}\) when the potential difference is 1.2 V.

stem:
The current drawn by the ammeter is maximum if:

(The figure shows two parallel branches connected between the same two nodes, with a source V, a series resistor R and an ideal ammeter in the main line. The top branch is three resistors in series, each with a switch: \(S_2\)–\(4\,\Omega\), \(S_4\)–\(5\,\Omega\), \(S_6\)–\(6\,\Omega\). The bottom branch is three resistors in series, each with a switch: \(S_1\)–\(1\,\Omega\), \(S_3\)–\(2\,\Omega\), \(S_5\)–\(3\,\Omega\). A branch conducts only when all three of its switches are closed.)

In which of the following networks of resistors is the equivalent resistance between points A and B highest?

(Network (i): from A, a series path of \(1\,\text{k}\Omega\) then \(200\,\Omega\) reaches B; a separate \(1\,\text{k}\Omega\) resistor connects A directly to B in parallel with that path. Network (ii): three resistors — \(1\,\text{k}\Omega\), \(200\,\Omega\) and \(1\,\text{k}\Omega\) — all connected in parallel between A and B. Network (iii): two \(1\,\text{k}\Omega\) resistors in parallel, then in series with a \(200\,\Omega\) resistor, between A and B.)

What is the equivalent resistance between points P and Q in the given circuit diagram?

(The figure shows an apex node T with two \(6\,\Omega\) resistors going down from T to nodes R and S respectively. R and S are also joined by a \(6\,\Omega\) resistor between them. From R a \(3\,\Omega\) resistor goes down to terminal P, and from S a \(3\,\Omega\) resistor goes down to terminal Q.)

Consider the following combinations of resistors. The combinations having equivalent resistance \(1\,\Omega\) is/are:

(Combination I: two \(2\,\Omega\) resistors in parallel. Combination II: three \(3\,\Omega\) resistors in parallel. Combination III: two parallel branches — top branch \(2\,\Omega\) and \(4\,\Omega\) in series, bottom branch \(3\,\Omega\) and \(3\,\Omega\) in series. Combination IV: two \(0.5\,\Omega\) resistors in parallel.)

Six equal resistances are connected between points P, Q and R as shown in the figure. The net resistance will be maximum between:

(The figure is a triangle with corners P (top), Q (bottom left) and R (bottom right). The side P–Q is a single resistor. The side P–R is three equal resistors in parallel. The side Q–R is two equal resistors in parallel. All six resistors have the same value.)
